sources.title: BattlEye Documentation - RCon commands and BEServer cfg settings
Multiplayer Server Commands - Bohemia Interactive Community wiki
dotFionn/arma3-rcon - BattlEye RCon client, players output fields
beCBL - BattlEye Community Ban List, bans.txt line format
Arma 3 RCON Terminal - BattlEye RCon command list and default port 2306

notes: Arma 3 is commanded over BattlEye RCon, a custom UDP protocol (single-datagram, CRC32-framed) - NOT Valve Source RCON, hence flavour "custom". BattlEye requires RConPort and RConPassword to be set explicitly in BattlEye/BEServer_x64.cfg (BEServer.cfg on 32-bit) and publishes no vendor default port; 2306 is the near-universal community convention (game port 2302 + 4) and is what RCon tooling defaults to. There is no separate enable setting - RCon is live once RConPassword is present, so enableSetting is null. kick and ban take the TRANSIENT player number from the left column of the players response, not the GUID: "kick [player #] [reason]" and "ban [player #] [time in minutes] [reason]", where 0 or an omitted time is permanent. The persistent identity is the 32-hex-character BattlEye GUID, captured as accountId by playerParse; use "addBan <GUID> <minutes> <reason>" to ban someone who is not connected. No unban template is recorded because removeBan takes a BAN INDEX from the bans command, not a player identifier - substituting a player id there would remove the wrong ban. Names of players still in the lobby are suffixed " (Lobby)" and GUIDs carry a (OK)/(?)/(-) verification suffix; both are stripped by linePattern. say -1 broadcasts to everyone; say <player #> whispers. There is no MOTD command over RCon (the MOTD is set by motd[] in server.cfg). Game-server commands prefixed with # (#shutdown, #lock, #userlist, #mission) are relayed through the same RCon socket, but the in-game admin commands #kick and #exec ban documented on the Multiplayer Server Commands wiki page are a separate channel typed into chat after #login and are not what this file sends. bans.txt lines are "<GUID or IP> <minutes remaining or -1> <reason>"; its location follows the -bepath launch argument when one is given.
